content:
After writing some HeapLang today I decided that we need a free variables linter iris-lean#451. I love our syntax, but I realize now that the Rocq version of sticking all of your variables in double quotes does make it a lot easier to see when a variable is free lol. My linter is partial, but I picture it catching common bugs of the following form:

  • Forgetting to & prefix a Lean term
  • Putting a space between a keyword and the left paren
  • Some of the hard to understand scopes, like how hl% λ l, &f l; &f l parses as hl% (λ l, &f l); &f l

Running on our codebase linter caught two bugs (of the last two kinds) in the HeapLang examples file! But I'm pretty sure also would have caught a lot of the annoying stuff I ran into while writing HeapLang examples today, and that's more how I imagine it being used.
This linter is great! I've enabled it by default and merged it. It would have also helped me a lot in the past, so I think it will be very useful.
